# apple_ci_products (Data Source)

Lists Xcode Cloud products. Create the product in Xcode first, then use its ID as `product_id` on `apple_ci_workflow`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_ci_products" "all" {}

output "products" {
  value = data.apple_ci_products.all.products
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `limit` (Number) The most records to return, between 1 and 200, after filtering and sorting.
- `name_pattern` (String) Return only records whose `name` matches this regular expression, matched as a substring unless anchored.
- `sort_by` (String) The attribute to sort by: `created_date`, `name`. Unset keeps Apple's order.
- `sort_order` (String) `asc` (the default) or `desc`. Has no effect without `sort_by`.

### Read-Only

- `filtered_count` (Number) How many records are returned, after filtering and the limit.
- `products` (Attributes List) The records that match, in the order asked for. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--products))
- `total_count` (Number) How many records Apple returned, before filtering.

<a id="nestedatt--products"></a>
### Nested Schema for `products`

Read-Only:

- `created_date` (String) When the product was created in Xcode Cloud, in ISO 8601.
- `id` (String) Apple's ID for the record, which `apple_ci_workflow` takes as a relationship.
- `name` (String) The product's name, as Xcode Cloud shows it: normally the app or framework target.
- `product_type` (String) What the product builds: `APP` or `FRAMEWORK`.
